title: Warnings to Judah and Its Neighbors
overview: The prophet urges Judah to turn to the LORD before judgment arrives, then announces that the surrounding nations will fall too, from the Philistine coast to the great city of Nineveh.

parts.label: Last call to Judah (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Judah is told to come together and take a hard look at itself before the day of the LORD's anger sweeps it away. The humble who already try to live rightly are urged to keep seeking God, though they are told only that they may be sheltered, not that they surely will be.

parts.label: The Philistine coast (vv. 4-7)
parts.note: Four Philistine cities west of Judah are named, with wordplay in Hebrew on names like Gaza and Ekron. Their crowded land will become empty pasture for Judah's survivors.

parts.label: Moab and Ammon (vv. 8-11)
parts.note: These neighbors east of the Jordan had mocked Judah and pushed into its land, so they are told they will become barren salt flats like Sodom and Gomorrah. The passage also pictures the gods of the nations losing their power and distant peoples worshiping the LORD in their own lands, which Christians later read as pointing to faith spreading worldwide.

parts.label: Cush in the far south (v. 12)
parts.note: Cush was the region south of Egypt, roughly today's Sudan, whose kings had not long before ruled Egypt. Some scholars think the name stands for Egypt as a whole here, though this is uncertain.

parts.label: The fall of Nineveh (vv. 13-15)
parts.note: Nineveh, capital of Assyria, the superpower that had dominated Judah, is pictured as a ruin where flocks graze and owls call through broken windows. The proud city that thought it had no equal did fall in 612 BC, and its ruins lay buried for centuries.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether this day of the LORD was fully fulfilled in the ancient conquests that swept the region, or also points ahead to a final judgment of the world.
think: Verse 3 offers the humble no guarantee of protection, only a hope; how do you think about doing right when there is no promise it will keep you safe?
